metadata.title: AI Roadmap v3: Zero to Advanced (100% Free Resources)
metadata.core_philosophy: Do not rush the math and the build it from scratch steps. They are what separate people who use AI from people who understand it.

rules: Every phase ends with a project on GitHub. No project, no moving on.
Implement at least one algorithm from scratch per phase (NumPy only), then use the library version.
Read one paper per week from Phase 5 onward.
Track progress in this web app and your GitHub repo README.
self_check_gates: End of each phase: explain the core idea out loud or in a short blog post without notes.
End of each phase: rebuild one piece (a metric, a layer, a pipeline step) from a blank file.
If you cannot do both, spend one more week on that phase before moving on.

breakdown: 3 sessions x 2 hrs: Course lectures plus code along
1 session x 1 hr: Paper reading or writing up what you learned
Weekend: Kaggle notebook or from scratch implementation

first_30_days.tasks: Watch 3Blue1Brown Linear Algebra and Neural Networks series. Start CS50P or skim Python if you already know it. Set up Git, GitHub, uv, and Google Colab.
Kaggle Learn: Python, Pandas. Start Khan Academy Statistics. Begin Andrew Ng's Machine Learning Specialization, Course 1.
Continue Ng's course. Kaggle Learn: Intro to ML. Publish your first EDA notebook.
Finish Ng's Course 1. Implement linear regression from scratch in NumPy. Start StatQuest ML playlist alongside.

Modern Python environment management with uv and linting with ruff
Git and GitHub workflows
Jupyter Notebook and Google Colab (free GPU)
Linux command line

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Build a CLI data parser and validator using pure Python classes, file handling, and custom iterators.
projects: Write a 200 line Python program with classes, type annotations, and file handling without looking up syntax constantly, hosted on GitHub with a uv lockfile.
phases.done_when: You can write a 200 line Python program with classes and file handling without looking things up constantly.

phases.title: Math for AI
topics: Linear Algebra: vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, SVD, PCA foundations
Calculus: derivatives, partial derivatives, chain rule, gradients (core of backpropagation)
Probability and Statistics: distributions, Bayes theorem, expectation, variance, MLE, hypothesis testing
Optimization basics: gradient descent, convexity, learning rates

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Write matrix multiplication, SVD/PCA via eigendecomposition, and numerical gradient checking in pure NumPy.
projects: Publish a Jupyter notebook implementing PCA and multivariate gradient descent from scratch with Matplotlib contour visualizations.
phases.done_when: You can derive gradient descent for linear regression by hand and explain what a gradient is.

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Implement custom Z-score outlier removal, missing value imputation, and correlation matrices using only NumPy arrays.
projects: Pick a real-world Kaggle dataset, perform a comprehensive Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), and publish the notebook publicly.
phases.done_when: You can take a messy raw dataset, clean it, run SQL/Pandas aggregations, and surface 3 actionable insights with clean charts.

phases.title: Classical Machine Learning
topics: Linear and Logistic Regression
k-NN, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVM)
Decision Trees, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM)
Unsupervised: k-means, Hierarchical Clustering, PCA, t-SNE, UMAP
Bias-variance tradeoff, cross-validation, regularization (L1/L2)
Evaluation metrics: precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC
Feature engineering and handling imbalanced data

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Implement linear regression, logistic regression, k-NN, a decision tree, and k-means using only NumPy.
projects: End-to-end House Price Prediction (regression with feature engineering)
Customer Churn or Fraud Detection (classification on imbalanced data with precision/recall tuning)
Enter one beginner Kaggle competition (Titanic, then a Tabular Playground Series)
phases.done_when: You have built the 5 core ML algorithms in pure NumPy and submitted a pipeline to a live Kaggle leaderboard.

phases.title: Deep Learning: ANN, CNN, RNN
topics: Perceptron, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN/MLP), activation functions, loss functions
Backpropagation: derive by hand, then implement in code
Optimizers: SGD, momentum, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW, learning rate schedules
Regularization: dropout, batch norm, layer norm, weight decay, early stopping
Weight initialization, vanishing and exploding gradients
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN): LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, EfficientNet, ConvNeXt
Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), LSTM, GRU, sequence modeling
Frameworks: PyTorch (primary), TensorFlow/Keras (secondary)

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Build a 2-layer neural network with manual backpropagation in NumPy, then build a CNN in PyTorch.
projects: MNIST then CIFAR-10 classification (compare MLP vs custom CNN)
Time-series forecasting with LSTM/GRU
Reproduce a miniature ResNet with skip connections on a small dataset
phases.done_when: You can write the backward pass of a linear + ReLU + CrossEntropy layer without autograd and train a PyTorch model on GPU.

Seq2Seq and the Attention mechanism
The Transformer Architecture: Self-Attention, Multi-Head Attention, Positional Encoding (RoPE), KV Caching
Encoder vs Decoder models: BERT vs GPT
Text classification, Named Entity Recognition (NER), summarization, translation, Q&A

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Implement Scaled Dot-Product Attention, Multi-Head Attention, and a Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer from scratch.

Build and train a character/subword-level mini-GPT from scratch on a custom text corpus
Build a document summarization or Q&A pipeline using Hugging Face Transformers

projects: Train a custom object detector with YOLO on your own labeled dataset
Medical or document image classifier using ViT or ResNet transfer learning
Real-time webcam application with OpenCV and PyTorch
phases.done_when: You have trained and evaluated a custom object detection or segmentation model on custom data.

phases.title: LLMs, Agents, and Generative AI
topics: LLM internals: pretraining, scaling laws, instruction tuning (SFT), RLHF, DPO, GRPO (reasoning models)
Prompt engineering, Context Engineering, and structured outputs (Pydantic)
Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: LoRA, QLoRA, PEFT, Unsloth
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): vector databases, embeddings, hybrid chunking, evaluation (RAGAS)
AI Agents: tool use, function calling, multi-step planning, Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Generative vision models: VAEs, GANs, Diffusion Models (Stable Diffusion, Flux)
Running quantized models locally (Ollama, llama.cpp)

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Implement a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) linear layer wrapper in pure PyTorch and a vector cosine-similarity retriever in NumPy.

Train a miniature diffusion model (DDPM) on a toy image dataset
phases.done_when: You have fine-tuned an open-weights LLM with QLoRA, built an MCP-enabled agent, and evaluated a RAG pipeline.

Paper reproduction methodology (ResNet, Attention Is All You Need, DDPM, LoRA)
Competitive ML & Hackathons: Kaggle, Hugging Face Hackathons, Zindi
Open-source contributions: scikit-learn, Hugging Face, PyTorch good first issues
Technical writing and portfolio curation

phases.from_scratch_exercise: Reproduce the core architecture and key ablation table of a landmark arXiv paper from scratch in PyTorch.
projects: Reproduce 2 to 3 landmark papers (e.g., ResNet, Attention Is All You Need, DDPM, LoRA)
Publish 3 technical blog posts explaining what you built
Curate a public portfolio of 5 to 7 strong deployed GitHub projects with clear READMEs, architecture diagrams, and live demos
phases.done_when: You have 5+ deployed portfolio projects, 3 technical articles, and 1 reproduced research paper on your GitHub.

One model deployed publicly with Docker and FastAPI
